question: The fat in chocolate, cocoa butter, melts at about 34 degrees Celsius. Why is that exactly the right temperature for a chocolate bar?
source_excerpt: cocoa butter is solid at room temperature but begins to melt around 93 °F, which is below average human body temperature.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone has felt chocolate melt in their mouth, but few realise it happens because its fat melts at a temperature just below our own body's.
extra.verification_notes: Cocoa butter Form V melts ~33.8 °C, just below body temperature (~37 °C), so it stays solid at room temperature and melts in the mouth.

explanation: Your mouth is about 37 degrees, so cocoa butter stays solid in the wrapper and turns liquid on your tongue. That silky melt is basic physics, timed to the human body.

question: The gummy-bear brand Haribo is built from three pairs of letters: the founder's first name, his surname and his home town. The founder was Hans Riegel. Which German city gives the 'BO'?
source_excerpt: Haribo is a syllabic abbreviation formed from Hans Riegel Bonn.

extra.why_interesting: Players treat 'Haribo' as a made-up, playful brand word and never suspect it hides a person and a city. Once the pattern is laid out, the last syllable becomes a small, solvable puzzle: a German city starting with 'Bo'. Many players will reach Bonn, the former West German capital, with an 'of course!' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Haribo is formed from Hans Riegel Bonn, so BO comes from Bonn (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haribo).

explanation: HA for Hans, RI for Riegel, BO for Bonn, the city where he started making sweets in his kitchen in 1920. So every bag of gold bears quietly carries a former capital of West Germany in its name.
